findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() can now return null, breaking callers that unbox the Long
findings.body: `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the underlying group can no longer be loaded from the store (concurrent deletion). `GroupModel#getSubGroupsCount()` is declared as `Long` but every other provider implementation returns a real count, and consumers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount()` forward the value straight into `GroupRepresentation#setSubGroupCount(...)`; any caller that compares or unboxes the value (e.g. `count > 0`, assignment to `long`) will now throw a NullPointerException instead of the original one, i.e. the NPE is only moved. It also silently produces representations with a missing/null `subGroupCount`, which the admin console uses for lazy-loading sub-groups. Prefer a defined behaviour for a vanished group: return `0L`, or follow the pattern used elsewhere in this class (`getDelegateForUpdate()` / registering an invalidation) so the stale cache entry is dropped.

findings.title: Same concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads
findings.body: The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without a null check. `modelSupplier` resolves to `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId())`, which returns `null` exactly in the scenario this PR fixes (group removed by another transaction while a stale `CachedGroup` entry is still served). Listing sub-groups concurrently with a group deletion therefore still produces a NullPointerException / HTTP 500, so the fix is incomplete and the added test only covers the count path.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined and can outlive/hang the test
findings.body: The test starts a plain (non-daemon) thread that loops on `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` until `deletedAll` is set, but it is never joined. Consequences: (1) `deletedAll` is only set at the end of the happy path, so if any `group(groupUuid).remove()` call throws, the flag is never set and the non-daemon thread spins forever issuing admin requests, hanging the build; (2) the thread keeps issuing requests against the shared `managedRealm` after this test method returns, which can interfere with subsequent tests and with realm cleanup. Set the flag in a `finally` block and `join()` the thread (with a timeout) before leaving the test.

findings.title: Assertion on caughtExceptions races with the reader thread, so the test can pass vacuously
findings.body: `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` is executed immediately after `deletedAll.set(true)` without any synchronization with the reader thread. Exceptions added by the reader after this point (including the very NPE this PR fixes, which is most likely to occur during the last deletions) are never observed, and if the reader thread had not yet issued a request overlapping a deletion the list is trivially empty. The result is a test that is both flaky and able to pass even when the regression is present; join the thread before asserting.
